I am 75 years old now, and I have been farming these fields in Quzhou since I was a young man. I never went to school, but I know my land better than any book. My son works in the city, so it is mostly me and my wife managing the crops now. I have about 8 mu of land in total. I do not want to take big risks at my age, so I will stick to what has always fed us: wheat and maize on 5 mu in rotation, and cotton on the other 3 mu. The wheat-maize double crop is our insurance — even if one does poorly, the other usually saves the year. Cotton gives good cash when the price is right, but it needs too much hand labor, so I keep it to 3 mu.

For the winter wheat, I will plant around the tenth month, same as my neighbors. I use the improved seed from the shop — not the most expensive kind, but reliable. I plow with the rotary tiller first to break up the stubble. For fertilizer, I put down about one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, and then I topdress with another half bag when the wheat starts jointing in spring. I also spread some ammonium bicarbonate — about one bag per mu. My neighbor Old Wang says four irrigations is enough if the winter snow is decent, so I will water four times: once at planting, once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray for weeds once and for insects twice, and if I see rust I will add a fungicide spray.

For the summer maize, there is no time to waste after wheat harvest in early June. I plant the hybrid maize right away — no tillage, just direct seeding with the machine while the wheat stubble is still warm. Maize does not need as much fertilizer as wheat. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and that is usually enough. I irrigate twice: once right after planting and once at the big trumpet leaf stage. I watch out for armyworms and weeds, so I spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. Last year I also used a plant regulator twice to keep the stalks short and strong.

For cotton, I plant in mid-to-late April. I rotary till the 3 mu and sow the improved cotton seed. Cotton needs more care. I use about one bag of compound fertilizer as basal, and another bag later when the buds start forming. I irrigate twice — once at flowering and once at boll formation. The bollworms are the big enemy, so I spray insecticide almost every week during summer, maybe 12 or 13 times in total, plus one herbicide spray and maybe one fungicide if the leaves turn spotty.

I expect about 800 jin of wheat per mu, 900 jin of maize per mu, and 550 jin of seed cotton per mu. I would rather apply a little too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than wasting a few yuan on extra urea. This is what I will do.
